# Sirach Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 2

---

1 My child, if you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for testing.

2 Set your heart right and be steadfast; do not be hasty in a time of calamity.

3 Cling to him and do not turn away, so that you may be honored at the end of your days.

4 Accept whatever is brought upon you, and in the changes that humble you, be patient.

5 For gold is tested in fire, and those acceptable to God in the furnace of humiliation.

6 Trust in him and he will help you; make your paths straight and hope in him.

7 You who fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; do not stray from him lest you fall.

8 You who fear the Lord, trust him, and your reward will not fail to come.

9 You who fear the Lord, hope for what is good — for everlasting gladness and mercy.

10 Look to the ancient generations and see: who has ever trusted in the Lord and been put to shame? Who has persevered in the fear of him and been abandoned? Who has called on him and been ignored?

11 For the Lord is compassionate and merciful; he forgives sins and rescues in the time of trouble.

12 Woe to faint hearts and slack hands, and to the sinner who walks two ways.

13 Woe to the despairing heart, which has no faith — therefore it will find no shelter.

14 Woe to you who have lost your endurance! What will you do when the Lord comes to reckon with you?

15 Those who fear the Lord do not disobey his words; those who love him keep his ways.

16 Those who fear the Lord seek to please him; those who love him are filled with his law.

17 Those who fear the Lord prepare their hearts and humble their souls before him.

18 Let us fall into the hands of the Lord rather than into the hands of mortals, for as his greatness is, so too is his mercy.

---

## Council Notes

**On v.3 "cling to him and do not depart":** EMET's rendering is memorable and literal. The Greek antechou autou = "cling, hold fast." This is one of the most important verses of the chapter; SOPHIA retains the vivid "cling."

**On v.5 "furnace of humiliation":** All agents agreed. The Greek kaminos tapeinōseōs is a striking image. Ben Sira deliberately parallels the gold-refining image with human suffering. PNEUMA's "hardship" is too vague; "humiliation" retained.

**On vv.7-9 refrain structure:** Ben Sira uses a three-fold address, "You who fear the Lord." SOPHIA preserves the structural repetition, which is rhetorical and intentional.

**On v.10 triple rhetorical question:** All agents rendered this well. PNEUMA's colloquial "ignored" for epeskiasē ("overlooked/passed by") is acceptable but SOPHIA prefers "ignored" as it carries the right sense of being dismissed.

**On v.18 "majesty/greatness":** EMET uses "majesty," LOGOS/PNEUMA "greatness." Greek megalōsynē = greatness/majesty. Both are accurate; "greatness" chosen for parallelism with "mercy."
